newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen opening lower on weaker bonds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen opening lower on weaker bonds.

text.p: * Toronto stocks were expected to open under pressure as Canadian bonds and bills weakened. * Analysts said gold stocks may bounce today after the bullion price stabilized overnight.
Toronto stocks were expected to open under pressure and face a choppy day as Canadian bonds and bills weighed on the market and gold stocks looked set for a possible bounce.

"Gold has stabilized, which is a good sign, but we've got our bonds and bills under pressure this morning, and that's going to be a pressure on the stock market," said MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie.
She said investors may use the pause in bullion's steep fall to pick up gold stocks, which have been hit by selling in recent sessions.
"So we may get a bit of a bounce in the gold sector but we'll get the financial sector under pressure," she said.
Bonds were under profit-taking pressure after an impressive day on Monday and were further weakened by the Canadian dollar, which softened overnight.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index fell 56.32 points on Monday to close at 6529.12 after New York's Comex gold price ended at 12-year lows. The US$6.20 an ounce drop in the gold price to US$319.00 dragged Barrick Gold Corp and Placer Dome Inc, Canada's two largest mining firms, to new 52-week lows.
